title.en: Brazil, 1964–1985: dictatorship and contested memory
title.zh: 1964—1985年巴西：独裁与记忆之争

location.label: Brasília; representative federal political center

summary.en:
Brazil’s military regime combined control of political institutions with surveillance and repression of opponents. Its history cannot be reconstructed only from the statements of presidents and generals. The National Archives holds records from state agencies alongside collections donated by persecuted people and their families, creating a basis for examining how repression reached workplaces, universities and everyday life.

Censorship and violence coexisted with cultural production and organizing that challenged official accounts. The transition to civilian rule in 1985 changed the governing arrangement but did not end disputes over accountability, missing people and access to records. Later truth-seeking initiatives made the preservation and interpretation of archives part of democratic politics. The regime’s national reach and the different experiences of local communities must be distinguished; one capital-city pin is only a point of orientation.
summary.zh:
巴西军事政权把政治机构控制，同监视及镇压反对者结合起来。不能只依总统和将军的声明重建其历史。国家档案馆既保存国家机构文书，也接收受迫害者及家属捐赠的收藏，为研究镇压如何进入工作场所、大学和日常生活提供基础。

审查和暴力，与挑战官方叙述的文化创作及组织行动并存。1985年转向文职统治改变治理安排，却没有终止问责、失踪者及档案开放的争论。后来的真相追寻，使档案保存和解释成为民主政治的一部分。需要区分政权的全国影响与各地社群的不同经历；首都地图点只是方位参照。

title.en: Bolivia, 1952–1953: revolution, land and citizenship
title.zh: 1952—1953年玻利维亚：革命、土地与公民身份

location.label: La Paz; representative political center

summary.en:
Bolivia’s 1952 revolution brought the Movimiento Nacionalista Revolucionario to power amid worker and popular mobilization. Changes in political participation and the nationalization of major mines challenged an order organized around restricted citizenship, concentrated landholding and powerful mining interests. The revolution’s meaning depended on what workers and rural communities could make of these new openings.

The 1953 agrarian reform followed pressure from Indigenous peasants and the occupation of estates. Land redistribution, unions and altered labour relations changed parts of the countryside, but implementation and later results varied. New legislation could dismantle some forms of servitude without eliminating every inequality or recognizing every Indigenous political aspiration. Research on fiscal institutions and agrarian change shows why the revolution must be followed into workplaces and communities, rather than ending the story with the replacement of a government.
summary.zh:
1952年，工人及民众动员中的玻利维亚革命，使民族革命运动掌权。政治参与变化和主要矿山国有化，挑战限制公民身份、土地集中及矿业巨头主导的秩序。革命的意义，取决于工人与乡村社群能够如何运用新机会。

1953年土地改革发生于原住民农民施压和占领庄园之后。土地再分配、工会及劳动关系变化，改变部分乡村，但实施和后续结果各异。新法可以拆解某些农奴式关系，却不能消除全部不平等或满足全部原住民族政治诉求。财政机构与土地变化研究说明，必须把革命追踪到工作场所和社群，而非以政府更替结束叙述。

dateNote.en: Focus on 1952 revolution and 1953 agrarian reform; later implementation is not compressed into these two years.

title.en: Guatemala, 1996: peace agreements and unfinished tasks
title.zh: 1996年危地马拉：和平协议与未完成的任务

location.label: Guatemala City; representative signing location

summary.en:
Guatemala’s government and the Unidad Revolucionaria Nacional Guatemalteca signed the Agreement on a Firm and Lasting Peace on 29 December 1996. It concluded a series of negotiations and agreements addressing an armed conflict that had devastated the country for more than three decades. The settlement joined the cessation of fighting to commitments concerning institutions, rights and participation.

Signing peace did not restore lives lost or automatically resolve the conditions that had sustained violence. Indigenous communities’ experiences of land, exclusion and state power remained central to the meaning of implementation. The archive of agreements permits readers to distinguish the promises made from the subsequent history of fulfilling them. Rigoberta Menchú’s advocacy connects this national milestone to international efforts to recognize Indigenous rights and social justice without making one person stand for every Maya community’s experience.
summary.zh:
1996年12月29日，危地马拉政府与危地马拉全国革命联盟签署《牢固持久和平协议》，完成一系列谈判和协议，为摧残国家三十多年的武装冲突画下节点。安排把停止战斗同机构、权利及参与承诺相连。

签署和平没有使逝者复生，也不会自动解决维持暴力的条件。原住民社群关于土地、排斥及国家权力的经历，仍是理解落实过程的核心。协议档案使读者能够区分作出的承诺与后来履行承诺的历史。里戈韦塔·门楚的倡议，把这一全国节点同国际原住民族权利和社会正义努力相连，但不能用一个人代表所有玛雅社群的经历。

dateNote.en: Final agreement signed 29 December 1996; earlier agreements and later implementation have separate dates.

title.en: Pachacuti · Reorganizing an expanding Inca state
title.zh: 帕查库蒂 · 重组扩张中的印加国家

location.label: Cusco; representative royal and administrative center

summary.en:
Pachacuti is associated with the transformation of Cusco’s rulers into an expanding imperial power during the fifteenth century. Political narratives connect his accession with conflict against the Chancas, while the reorganization of Cusco linked rule to a capital with sacred, administrative and productive functions. Expansion drew on conquest, alliances and the incorporation of existing local authorities.

The traditions about him were written down after the Spanish conquest and do not supply an uncontested modern-style life chronology. Conventional reign dates are therefore a reference for comparison, not proof of a precise annual frontier. His significance extends beyond military victories to the organization of a diverse Andean political world. The institutions attributed to imperial rule also depended on practices developed by earlier societies. Comparing his story with regional archaeology prevents a ruler’s biography from absorbing the history of every people incorporated into Tawantinsuyu.
summary.zh:
帕查库蒂与十五世纪库斯科统治者向帝国强权的转变有关。政治叙述把他即位同对昌卡人的冲突相连，库斯科重组则把统治同具有神圣、行政及生产功能的都城联系起来。扩张依赖征服、联盟及对既有地方权威的纳入。

关于他的传统在西班牙征服后才被写下，不能提供没有争议的现代式生平年表。传统统治年代因此是比较参照，而非精确逐年边界的证明。其重要性超出战功，也涉及组织多样的安第斯政治世界。帝国制度还依赖更早社会发展的实践。把个人故事同区域考古比较，可避免统治者传记吞没被纳入塔万廷苏尤的各族历史。

dateNote.en: Working reign focus c.1438–1471 follows the British Museum; other surveys extend to c.1473. These are not birth/death dates.

title.en: Guaman Poma · An Andean critique of colonial government
title.zh: 关曼·波马 · 安第斯人的殖民治理批评

location.label: Lucanas region; representative manuscript setting

summary.en:
Felipe Guaman Poma de Ayala assembled an illustrated chronicle that joined Andean histories to a critique of Spanish colonial government. His account addressed the king of Spain and described the harms and contradictions of the new order. Pictures and text gave Indigenous perspectives a form that challenged histories written mainly by Spanish observers.

In a February 1615 letter he reported that his chronicle was complete. The surviving manuscript, held by the Royal Danish Library, contains more than a thousand pages and hundreds of drawings. It is not a transparent record of every Andean experience: its author had positions, purposes and an argument about good government. Reading it critically nevertheless restores a named Indigenous intellectual to the history of colonial knowledge. Digitization now permits the manuscript’s sequence of images and words to be studied rather than treating individual illustrations as context-free pictures.
summary.zh:
费利佩·关曼·波马·德·阿亚拉编成插图编年史，把安第斯历史同对西班牙殖民治理的批评结合。他向西班牙国王陈述新秩序的伤害与矛盾，图文为原住民立场提供形式，挑战主要由西班牙观察者书写的历史。

他在1615年2月的信中报告编年史已经完成。丹麦皇家图书馆保存的手稿有一千多页及数百幅画作，但不是每个安第斯人经历的透明记录：作者有自己的立场、目的和“善政”论述。批判阅读仍能把一位具名原住民知识人重新纳入殖民知识史。数字化使人们可以研究图文顺序，而非把单幅插图当成没有语境的图片。

dateNote.en: Documented writing focus c.1585–1615, not an asserted lifespan; birth and death dates vary across scholarship.
dateNote.zh: 约1585—1615年为写作观察窗口，不作为生卒年；研究对出生及死亡时间有不同判断。

title.en: Túpac Amaru II · Rebellion against colonial exploitation
title.zh: 图帕克·阿马鲁二世 · 反抗殖民剥削

location.label: Tinta region; representative rebellion setting

summary.en:
José Gabriel Condorcanqui adopted the name Túpac Amaru II while leading a rebellion against colonial rule in 1780. Complaints about officials, tribute and coercive labour belonged to a wider world of Andean grievances. His position as a local Indigenous authority and his invocation of Inca ancestry shaped the language through which rebellion could attract support.

The movement drew different groups whose aims were not identical. Armed conflict spread through southern Peru and into the wider Andean region, with alliances, violence and changing demands. Colonial authorities captured and executed Túpac Amaru II in 1781, but rebellion did not end with his death. Later movements remembered his name in different ways. His biography connects the structures of colonial extraction to political imagination and collective action without making every rebel’s goal the same as that of its best-known leader.
summary.zh:
何塞·加夫列尔·孔多尔坎基在1780年领导反殖民起义时采用“图帕克·阿马鲁二世”之名。对官员、贡赋与强迫劳动的不满，属于更广泛的安第斯积怨。他作为地方原住民权威的地位，以及对印加祖先的援引，塑造动员支持的政治语言。

运动吸引目标并不相同的群体。武装冲突扩展于秘鲁南部及更广安第斯地区，伴随联盟、暴力和变化中的要求。殖民当局于1781年将他捕获并处决，但起义并未随其死亡结束。后来运动以不同方式纪念他的名字。其传记把殖民榨取结构同政治想象和集体行动相连，却不能把所有起义者目标等同于最著名领袖的目标。

title.en: Bartolina Sisa · Aymara leadership in anticolonial resistance
title.zh: 巴尔托莉娜·西萨 · 艾马拉反殖民抵抗的领导者

location.label: La Paz / surrounding Aymara region; representative resistance setting

summary.en:
Bartolina Sisa participated in the Aymara uprising associated with Túpac Katari and the siege of La Paz in 1781. Her leadership makes women visible within an anticolonial movement often narrated through male figures. Organizing food, people and resistance required relationships across communities as well as decisions made by named leaders.

She was captured during the conflict and executed by colonial authorities in 1782. Later Indigenous women’s movements made her a symbol of collective struggle, connecting the memory of colonial violence to demands for representation and dignity. That commemoration should not erase uncertainty about parts of her early life or turn every modern organization into an unchanged survival of an eighteenth-century institution. Her documented final years offer a connection between the broader Andean rebellions and the continuing political importance of Indigenous women’s historical memory.
summary.zh:
巴尔托莉娜·西萨参与与图帕克·卡塔里有关的艾马拉起义，以及1781年对拉巴斯的围攻。她的领导使女性在常以男性为中心的反殖民叙述中可见。组织食物、人群及抵抗，既依靠具名领袖的决定，也依靠跨社群关系。

她在冲突中被捕，1782年遭殖民当局处决。后来的原住民妇女运动将她作为集体斗争象征，把殖民暴力记忆同代表权及尊严诉求连接起来。但纪念不能抹去其早年部分细节的不确定性，也不能把现代组织都当成十八世纪制度未经改变的存续。她有据可查的最后几年，连接更广的安第斯起义与原住民女性历史记忆持续的政治意义。

title.en: Gabriela Mistral · Poetry, teaching and public work
title.zh: 加夫列拉·米斯特拉尔 · 诗歌、教育与公共工作

location.label: Vicuña / Elqui Valley; representative formative region

summary.en:
Gabriela Mistral, born Lucila Godoy Alcayaga, connected poetry with teaching and public service. Her work as an educator and her writing about children, loss and belonging emerged from Chilean settings but reached readers across borders. In 1922 she went to Mexico to contribute to educational reform and popular libraries, linking literary activity with practical questions about access to learning.

International teaching, cultural work and diplomacy broadened her public career. The 1945 Nobel Prize in Literature recognized a writer who had already worked across national institutions and audiences. Her life cannot be reduced to one national monument or to the prize alone. Reading poems alongside educational work restores a dimension of Latin American intellectual history in which women addressed schools, social inequality and the responsibilities of public culture.
summary.zh:
加夫列拉·米斯特拉尔本名露西拉·戈多伊·阿尔卡亚加，把诗歌同教学及公共服务连接起来。教育工作及关于儿童、失落和归属的写作，源于智利经历，却跨越国界获得读者。1922年，她赴墨西哥参与教育改革与大众图书馆建设，把文学活动同学习机会的实际问题相连。

国际教学、文化工作与外交扩大她的公共生涯。1945年诺贝尔文学奖表彰的，是一位早已跨越国家机构及读者群工作的作家。不能把她的一生缩减为民族纪念物或一个奖项。结合诗歌和教育工作，可恢复拉美知识史中女性讨论学校、社会不平等及公共文化责任的面向。

dateNote.zh: 生卒年1889—1957；墨西哥教育工作始于1922年，1945年获诺贝尔奖。

title.en: Frida Kahlo · Painting body, identity and Mexico
title.zh: 弗里达·卡洛 · 绘写身体、身份与墨西哥

location.label: Casa Azul, Coyoacán; representative home and studio

summary.en:
Frida Kahlo made paintings that joined bodily experience, personal relationships and Mexican cultural forms. Her self-portraits cannot be separated from disability and pain, but they were also deliberate artistic constructions rather than medical records. Clothing, jewelry, plants and objects helped her present identities in conversation with post-revolutionary Mexico and international artistic networks.

The Casa Azul and surviving personal belongings offer evidence alongside the paintings. Medical devices could be decorated, and garments could both support or conceal a body and communicate cultural choices. Later exhibitions have examined these materials rather than treating her image only as a commercial icon. Kahlo’s career included teaching and exhibitions as well as life with Diego Rivera. Her history connects the making of art to gender, embodiment and political culture without making every painted symbol a literal statement about one event in her biography.
summary.zh:
弗里达·卡洛的绘画把身体经历、私人关系与墨西哥文化形式结合。自画像离不开残疾与疼痛，却也是有意构造的艺术，而非病历。衣饰、植物与物品，帮助她在革命后墨西哥及国际艺术网络中呈现身份。

蓝屋和保存的私人物品，为绘画之外提供证据。医疗支具可以被装饰，服装既可支撑或遮掩身体，也能表达文化选择。后来的展览研究这些材料，而非只把她的形象当作商业符号。卡洛的生涯包含教学与展览，也包含同迭戈·里韦拉的生活。她的历史把艺术创作同性别、身体和政治文化相连，不能把每个绘画符号都当作某次生平事件的字面陈述。

title.en: Rigoberta Menchú · Indigenous rights across borders
title.zh: 里戈韦塔·门楚 · 跨越国界的原住民族权利

location.label: Chimel / Guatemalan highlands; representative community reference

summary.en:
Rigoberta Menchú Tum brought K’iche’ and wider Indigenous rights into international debate during Guatemala’s armed conflict. Her public advocacy connected rural inequality, violence and exclusion to the question of whose experiences were heard by national and international institutions. In 1983 she narrated a life history to Elisabeth Burgos, producing a book that attracted attention beyond Guatemala.

The work is mediated testimony, not an unedited transcript or an account that can stand for every Maya community. Her 1992 Nobel Peace Prize recognized advocacy for social justice and Indigenous rights. Later campaigning and public work continued beyond the award and the 1996 peace settlement. Reading her biography with the peace agreements and living Maya histories connects an individual public voice to collective struggles without making recognition by an international institution the endpoint of those struggles.
summary.zh:
危地马拉武装冲突期间，里戈韦塔·门楚·图姆把基切人及更广原住民族权利带入国际讨论。她的倡议把乡村不平等、暴力和排斥，同国家及国际机构听取谁的经历相连。1983年，她向伊丽莎白·布尔戈斯讲述生命史，形成在危地马拉之外引发关注的书籍。

该作品是经过中介的见证，不是未编辑逐字稿，也不能代表每个玛雅社群。1992年诺贝尔和平奖表彰其社会正义和原住民族权利倡议。后来的运动及公共工作延续于获奖与1996年和平安排之后。结合传记、和平协议和活态玛雅历史，可把个人公共声音同集体斗争相连，而不以国际机构认可作为斗争终点。
